claims.head: Fresh legs against tired ones
claims.body: It’s the Bruins’ second game in two nights. Teams on the back end of those usually spend more time defending, so we think the Kings get more of the play than usual.
claims.call: The Kings get a bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances than they usually do.

claims.head: The Bruins’ edge in shot quality
claims.body: The Bruins are around the middle of the league for shot quality, and the Kings are the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.

notes.text: Jonathan Aspirot has been a scratch for the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Frédéric Brunet has taken his spot beside Mason Lohrei.
Connor Clifton has been a scratch for the last 2 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Will Borgen has taken his spot beside Nikita Zadorov.

They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 3 of their last 5 games, including the last one. Corey Perry takes shifts on two lines, L2 and L4. Joel Edmundson is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Doughty and Ceci.
Quinton Byfield is no longer killing penalties: 5% of the team’s shorthanded time in 5 games, down from 43% last season.

LAK.head: The Kings have a lot going for them
LAK.body: Boston is on the second night of a back-to-back, while Los Angeles has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage. The Bruins can make it interesting if they keep dangerous shots away.

BOS.head: The Bruins have a hill to climb
BOS.body: Boston is on the second night of a back-to-back, while Los Angeles has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage. The Bruins’ best way through is keeping dangerous shots away.

story.head: The Kings are still looking for their first win
paras: The Kings are still looking for their first win of the season, 0-3-2 through five games. The Bruins have won four straight.
The Bruins have the edge over the Kings on shot quality.
